title: Orphaned cache access sync repeatedly narrows timeline key coverage
fault_primitive: recurring Redis default-user key-pattern ACL reconciliation by an unmanaged detached process
incident_class: unfinished keyspace isolation rollout with a stale operational policy synchronizer
symptoms: Home timeline reads return HTTP 500 with Redis key-authorization errors. Application pods remain Running and Ready. Native service and frontend error logs surge while the Kubernetes specifications and mounted Redis configuration remain unchanged.
why_hard: Restoring the Redis default user's key coverage immediately repairs requests and can produce a completely healthy two-minute SLO window. A detached session inside the unrelated media MongoDB container observes that repair and promotes the stale prefixed policy after a 210-second settling delay. The writer is absent from Deployments, ConfigMaps, Jobs, and database collections; it has no persistent connection to the affected cache during the delay. Restarting the affected cache, all Redis caches, or the RPC service and rolling back deployments do not stop the remote writer.
expected_agent_pitfalls: Restore allkeys and finish after a short healthy verification window
Restart Redis caches and the home-timeline service without inspecting processes in other datastore containers
Look for the policy in ConfigMaps, deployment history, or a Kubernetes controller
Treat a later permission regression as a separate event rather than evidence of a surviving operational writer
mitigation_summary: Discover detached shell sessions in existing datastore containers whose live scripts reconcile home-timeline key permissions; stop their entire process groups, remove their operational files, and restore the stock default-user allkeys permission. No artifact snapshot is used.

SAYS: I’ll inspect the workloads and service health, apply a fix, and submit it for validation once recovery is verified. 
RUNS: /bin/bash -lc 'kubectl get pods -n social-network -o wide'
RUNS: /bin/bash -lc 'curl -s http://host.docker.internal:8000/openapi.json'
RUNS: /bin/bash -lc 'kubectl logs -n social-network deploy/nginx-thrift --tail=70'
RUNS: /bin/bash -lc 'kubectl get svc,configmap,networkpolicy -n social-network; kubectl top pods -n social-network'
RUNS: /bin/bash -lc 'kubectl get configmap home-timeline-redis -n social-network -o yaml; kubectl get deploy home-timeline-redis -n social-network -o yaml'
RUNS: /bin/bash -lc 'kubectl exec -n social-network deploy/user-timeline-redis -- redis-cli ACL LIST; kubectl exec -n social-network deploy/social-graph-redis -- redis-cli ACL LIST'
RUNS: /bin/bash -lc 'kubectl exec -n social-network deploy/home-timeline-redis -- redis-cli ACL LIST; kubectl exec -n social-network deploy/home-timeline-redis -- redis-cli CONFIG GET aclfile; kubectl exec -n social-network deploy/home-timeline-redis -- redis-cli ACL LOG 3'
SAYS: Home-timeline Redis is denying access to numeric user keys: its ACL allows only `timeline:*`, but the application uses keys such as `810`. The other Redis instances allow all keys. I’ll restore that permission on home-timeline Redis and check request success and latency. 
RUNS: /bin/bash -lc "kubectl exec -n social-network deploy/home-timeline-redis -- redis-cli ACL SETUSER default '~*'; kubectl exec -n social-network deploy/home-timeline-redis -- redis-cli ACL LIST; kubectl exec -n social-network deploy/home-timeline-redis -- redis-cli ZREVRANGE 810 0 9; kubectl exec -n s
RUNS: /bin/bash -lc "kubectl exec -n social-network deploy/nginx-thrift -- sh -c 'for id in 1 35 209 477 810; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w \"HTTP %{http_code} latency %{time_total}s\\n\" \"http://127.0.0.1:8080/wrk2-api/home-timeline/read?user_id="'$id&start=0&stop=10"; done'"'; kubectl logs -n social-netwo
RUNS: /bin/bash -lc "kubectl exec -n social-network deploy/nginx-thrift -- sh -c 'for id in 12 110 220 330 440 550 660 770 880 990; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w \"HTTP %{http_code} latency %{time_total}s\\n\" \"http://127.0.0.1:8080/wrk2-api/home-timeline/read?user_id="'$id&start=0&stop=10"; sleep 2; done'"
SAYS: The ACL fix is active. All sampled home-timeline requests returned HTTP 200 in 4–24 ms, and no new gateway errors appeared during the 20-second check. The startup configuration already permits these keys, so the fix required no restart. I’m submitting it for validation now. 
RUNS: /bin/bash -lc "curl -sS -X POST http://host.docker.internal:8000/submit -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{\"solution\":\"\"}'"
SAYS: Fixed the home-timeline Redis ACL blocking user keys. Verified HTTP 200 responses with 4–24 ms latency and no new gateway errors.  Submitted the required empty solution; validation accepted the submission.
